name: Uterovaginal Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification

criteria.description: Presence of congenital uterine and/or vaginal structural anomalies confirmed by imaging or surgery
Primary amenorrhea or dysmenorrhea associated with uterovaginal malformation
MRI or ultrasound evidence of uterine or vaginal agenesis, hypoplasia, or duplication
Surgical visualization confirming uterovaginal structural anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital uterine and/or vaginal structural anomaly confirmed by imaging or surgery
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including imaging and sometimes surgical confirmation.

laboratory: Normal hormonal profile in most cases
Elevated FSH/LH if gonadal dysgenesis present
imaging: MRI pelvis showing uterine and vaginal structural anomalies
Ultrasound demonstrating absent or hypoplastic uterus
Intravenous pyelogram or renal ultrasound for associated renal anomalies
genetic: No single gene mutation identified; possible multifactorial etiology
other: Psychological assessment for coping with infertility or sexual dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Absent uterus due to androgen receptor defect
Menstrual outflow obstruction without uterine agenesis
Identified by imaging and surgical exploration

redFlags: Severe cyclic pelvic pain indicating obstructed menstruation
